newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario regulator says probing Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Ontario regulator says probing Bre-X.

text.p: The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) said on Thursday that it is investigating whether Bre-X Minerals Ltd has breached disclosure rules or insider trading provisions.
Canada's biggest securities regulator said in a statement that it has been part of an ongoing investigation of Bre-X since the end of 1996.
But the OSC has not revealed details of the probe until today.
"The OSC can confirm that the investigation relates to whether there has been a breach of continuous disclosure requirements or insider trading provisions," the statement said.
The other players in the investigation are the Toronto Stock Exchange and Alberta Securities Commission (ASC).
The OSC said it has not determined whether there is sufficient evidence to warrant formal proceedings under Ontario's Securities Act.
Bre-X has been mired in controversy since preliminary drilling tests performed by its partner, Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc found little gold at the Busang site in Indonesia.
Dave Linder, senior enforcement counsel for the ASC in Calgary, confirmed that province's regulatory body was involved in the OSC probe, but declined to provide further details of the investigation.

"We have to provide some confidentiality over our investigations because if it turns out that everything's fine, we don't want to damage parties' reputations in the interim," Linder said in a telephone interview.
Bre-X began trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange in April 1996. It has traded on the Alberta Stock Exchange since 1989.
The OSC said it will work with the TSE and ASC to determine whether the Bre-X situation revealed any gaps in regulations.
"However, at present, the OSC does not see how greater regulation would have served to avoid recent developments in the Bre-X matter," the commission said.
